coaching_qa.query: Explain how mechanical tension drives muscle growth without using fluff.
coaching_qa.generated_output:
Mechanical tension is the primary driver of hypertrophy. It occurs when a muscle is forced to produce force under a load, stretching and contracting against resistance.

This tension activates mechanosensors in the muscle cell membrane, triggering anabolic signaling pathways (mTOR, MAPK). The key variables are load magnitude, time under tension, and stretch at long muscle lengths.

Lengthened partials and stretch pauses maximize tension on individual fibers by eliminating momentum and elastic recoil. This forces active recruitment, not passive bouncing. Without sufficient mechanical tension, other growth stimuli are largely irrelevant.
